statement: Let h = len(num)/2. Let SL = sum_{i=0}^{h-1} d(num[i]) and SR = sum_{i=h}^{len(num)-1} d(num[i]), where d(c)=c-48 if 48<=c<=57 and d(c)=0 otherwise. Let qL = count_{i=0}^{h-1}(num[i]=63) and qR = count_{i=h}^{len(num)-1}(num[i]=63). The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r = true if and only if 2*(SL-SR) != 9*(qR-qL). Equivalently, r = true exactly when Alice has a winning strategy in the game, and r = false exactly when Bob has a winning strategy.
preconditions: len(num) is even, 2 <= len(num) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(num), num[i] is either an ASCII digit byte (48 <= num[i] <= 57) or the ASCII byte for '?' (num[i] = 63).
